literal: Giving, living so that fame arises, other than that, profit there is not for the soul.
translation: To give to those in need and live a life of fame—besides this, there is no true gain for a living soul.
modern: ஏழைகளுக்குக் கொடுப்பதும் புகழுடன் வாழ்வதும் ஆகிய அதைத் தவிர, மனித உயிர்க்கு வேறு எந்த இலாபமும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet highlights the ultimate purpose of human existence. The poet asserts that giving to the needy (ītal) and living in a way that earns lasting fame (icaipaṭa vāḻtal) are the only true achievements. Any other material accumulation or success is not considered a real profit (ūtiyam) for the soul. The word 'icai' specifically denotes fame, emphasizing that a life remembered for its generosity is the only life of true value.
